title: Dick Advocaat resigns as Curacao manager months before nation’s World Cup debut
content:
Dick Advocaat has stepped down as Curacao manager three months after leading the nation to their first World Cup.

The national team announced via a statement on Monday that the 78-year-old was leaving the role to look after his daughter, who has health issues.

His resignation comes less than four months before Curacao make their World Cup debut at the 2026 tournament in the United States, Canada and Mexico, having become the smallest nation in the competition’s history to qualify.

Advocaat has been replaced by former PSV manager Fred Rutten, 63.

Advocaat took charge of Curacao in January 2024 and led the Caribbean island of 185,000 people to the World Cup after an unbeaten qualifying campaign.

Curacao went undefeated in a group consisting of Bermuda, Trinidad and Tobago and Jamaica. Their qualification — confirmed with a draw to Jamaica in November — meant they surpassed Iceland (with a population of 350,000) as the smallest nation to reach the World Cup.

“I have always said that family comes before football,” Advocaat said in a statement. “This is therefore a natural decision.

“That said, I will greatly miss Curacao, its people, and my colleagues. I consider qualifying the smallest nation in the world for the World Cup one of the highlights of my career. I am proud of my players, staff and board members who believed in us!”

The Dutchman has previously managed the Netherlands and South Korea at World Cup tournaments, in 1994 and 2006 respectively.

The president of the nation’s football federation said Curacao will “always remain grateful” to Advocaat and “his decision commands nothing but respect”.

Curacao will face Germany, Ivory Coast and Ecuador in Group E at this summer’s tournament. Their first match is on June 14 against Germany in Houston, Texas.
